    Say it like Skippy

    • "Aye, skipper." (to anyone he trusts)
    • "I gave my word. That's the end of it."
    • "Ah, you thought I'd smash it. I'm going to measure it."
    • "Touch iron." (before the cannon fires)

    Short and clear, a sea word now and then. Slow and quiet about the captain.

    Spells

    Cantrips are free. Each spell of level 1 or higher costs a slot. The Artillerist spells (Shield, Thunderwave, Scorching Ray, Shatter) are always ready.

    Shocking Grasp PHB p.275

    I touch a creature with lightning. On a hit it cannot take reactions until its next turn, so it cannot hit me as I walk away. Advantage if it wears metal armor.

    What the table sees (an idea, not a rule) He touches the enemy with the steel tip of his pliers. A blue spark cracks, like a struck flint.

    What each skill is for

    TRAINED (+3 in the number)

    Arcana +7 PHB p.177

    Remember things about magic: spells, magic items, strange symbols, other worlds.

    Inttrained

    Example: "What is this glowing rune on the door?"

    Investigation +7 PHB p.178

    Look for clues and work out what they mean: find a hidden latch, see what weapon made a wound, find the weak spot of a wall.

    Inttrained

    Example: Searching a captain's desk for a secret drawer.

    Athletics +4 PHB p.175

    Climb, jump, swim, and push or grab people. Also the check to shove or grapple in a fight.

    Strtrained

    Example: Climbing a ship's rigging in a storm.

    Spot, hear or notice things: an ambush, a sound behind a door, a ship on the horizon. Passive Perception 13 is used when I am not looking on purpose.

    Replicate Magic Item: what it can copy

    How it works T p.22-23

    Skippy knows Replicate Magic Item (learned at level 5 in place of Enhanced Weapon). The item is not picked yet: pick it in Edit Skippy › Infusions.

    • Each item is its own infusion: learning "bag of holding" does not give me "rope of climbing".
    • After a long rest I touch a plain object and it becomes that item. It counts as one of my 2 infused items.
    • Longer lists open at levels 6, 10 and 14.
    • I may also copy a common magic item from the Dungeon Master's Guide (not my book: ask the DM).
    knownitem still to pick

    The 8 items I could copy now T p.22-23

    • Alchemy jug: pours a liquid I pick each day (water, oil, wine...). Attunement: no.
    • Bag of holding: holds far more than its size and stays light. Attunement: no.
    • Cap of water breathing: breathe underwater. Attunement: no.
    • Goggles of night: see in the dark (I already have darkvision; they add range). Attunement: no.
    • Rope of climbing: a rope that moves, knots and ties itself on command. Attunement: no.
    • Sending stones: a pair of stones for a short message across any distance. Attunement: no.
    • Wand of magic detection: casts Detect Magic from its charges. Attunement: no.
    • Wand of secrets: points to the nearest hidden door or trap. Attunement: no.
    attunement: none

    Item details are in the Dungeon Master's Guide, not in my books. Ask the DM how each works.

    Swap rules

    Change which infusions I KNOW T p.12

    Each time I gain an artificer level, I can replace one infusion I know with another one I could learn. At level 5 I know 4. At level 6 I know 6.

    on level upone swap

    Change which items are ACTIVE T p.12-13

    After each long rest I can put a known infusion on a plain item by touching it. I can have 2 infused items at a time at level 5 (3 at level 6). Making one more ends the oldest.

    long rest

    One per item T p.12

    An item can carry only one of my infusions. If an infusion needs attunement, I can attune to the item at once.

    rule

    How long they last T p.13

    An infusion stays as long as I want. It ends if I make one too many (the oldest ends), if I swap out that infusion, or a few days after I die (as many days as my Int modifier).

    rule

    Example: Long sea trip: after a long rest, the homunculus rests and Replicate Magic Item makes a cap of water breathing instead.

    Skippy

    Half-orc Artificer 5 (Artillerist) · Pirate (Sailor variant) · chaotic neutral · 6,500 XP

    Languages: Common, Draconic · darkvision 60 ft · passive Perception 13

    Ex powder monkey of The Widow. Searching for Captain Edwine Blackscale, a bronze dragonborn. Companion: Mourning Bell, a Tiny bell-shaped black iron cannon with no legs, fired from the shoulder.

    Skippy

    Why "Skippy"? story

    The ship's captain was called "the skipper". The captain took him in as a small boy. The crew said "the skipper's boy", then "skipper's", then Skippy. He kept the name because it is the only thing the captain gave him.

    Backstory story

    Skippy never knew his parents. A half-orc child alone on the docks, he was about to be sent to a work house when the captain of The Widow bought his freedom with a bag of coins and a joke. The captain was a bronze dragonborn named Edwine Blackscale. The crew called her "the skipper".

    On the ship, Skippy was a powder monkey: the boy who runs gunpowder from the powder room to the cannons during a fight. Fast, hot, loud and dangerous. He learned every cannon by sound. The captain taught him charts and gadgets, and he learned to cast through his tools. The crew spoke Draconic, so he did too.

    Then came the storm and a rival ship's guns. The Widow went down in one night. Skippy woke on a beach with the ship's last cannon, a small bell-shaped black iron gun. Years later he found a way to shrink it with magic. Now it is his Eldritch Cannon, Mourning Bell.

    The captain was never found. Skippy does not believe she is dead. He maps every coast he visits and marks where she could have washed ashore.

    Why Bad Reputation and chaotic neutral? PHB p.139

    Port towns still remember The Widow and a half-orc with a cannon. They are afraid, so he gets away with small crimes. He is loyal to one person, not to rules: he will break any law to find the captain, but he will not break a promise.

    Looks story

    Age 22 · 6 ft 1 in · 210 lb · amber eyes · gray-green skin · black hair tied back with a rope end. Tall and lean, small tusks when he grins, old powder burns on his hands. Patched sailor's coat over a breastplate, a cloak that billows when he wants it to. Talks to his tools as if they were crew. On his shoulder: Mourning Bell, WIDOW stamped on the barrel.

    Personality

    Personality traits sheet

    • I keep my word like treasure, even with an enemy.
    • I hum the old songs of The Widow's crew while I work.

    Ideal sheet

    Loyalty (chaotic). A crew is a family. No law and no map is worth more than one person left behind.

    Bond sheet

    My captain is out there. I will find Edwine Blackscale, or find what happened to her, even if it takes my whole life.

    Flaw sheet

    I cannot stop looking at a map. If a coastline is blank, I will go and see it, even when the party needs me somewhere else.

    Lucky charm PHB p.139

    A small red coral horn (a horn charm against the evil eye) on a cord around his neck. He touches it when someone gives him the evil eye and before a risky shot. Story only: no rule effect.

    The captain

    Captain Edwine Blackscale PHB p.32-34

    Bronze dragonborn. Edwine is her own name. Blackscale is her pirate name, in the style of Blackbeard (the real pirate Edward Teach): the soot, smoke and grime of many battles darkened her bronze scales.

    • Breath: a line of lightning (Dex save); resists lightning damage.
    • Look: tall, battle-darkened bronze scales, green-gold eyes, a long scar on the left of her snout, a faded blue captain's coat, a brass spyglass.
    • Personality: booming, generous, a little vain. Terrible jokes. She never left a crew member behind, until the night The Widow sank.

    The Widow and Mourning Bell T p.17-18

    The Widow was her ship. Mourning Bell is the ship's last black iron gun, shrunk by magic. It tolls for the lost crew. It is Tiny with no legs: Skippy carries it on his shoulder and fires it like a rocket launcher.

    Language T p.7

    Skippy swaps Orc for Draconic with Tasha's Customizing Your Origin, because he grew up with her crew.

    Allies and DM

    Allies, enemies, mixed sheet

    Allies: the old crew of The Widow, scattered across the coast. Any harbor-master who owes the captain a favor.

    Enemies: the rival ship that sank The Widow (name it with the DM). A mapmakers' guild that sells false charts.

    Mixed: dragonborn sailors who knew the captain. Some help him. Some still blame her for the wreck.

    Questions for the DM story

    • Can the search for the captain enter the one-shot? A clue on a map, or a dragonborn stranger who knows the name?
    • May the rival ship, or the wreck of The Widow, be a place we can visit?
    • Can my cartographer's tools help draw a map during the game?
    • Is Bad Reputation known in this world, and does anyone remember The Widow?

    Hooks for the DM story

    • A torn page from the captain's logbook, with Blackscale's mark, in a hidden place.
    • A sailor in the tavern speaks Draconic and says they saw the captain, but wants a favor first.
    • A treasure chart with the captain's old coast marks. It might lead to the party's quest, or to a trap.

    Guide

      Plans, rules and notes for when you have a minute. Everything for play is on Play.

      Settings

      Sync and version

      Starting…

      Sync is off in this app. It needs your GitHub key once. Copy the key on this device (for example from your notes), then tap Paste key. Safari and the Home Screen app each need it once.

      The sync file is damaged or is not a Skippy save. If this iPhone has the right Skippy, send it to repair the file (the damaged file stays in the GitHub history).

      Version 2026.11.19-1152Update gets the newest version and syncs now.

      Skippy syncs by himself: when the app opens, when you come back to it, a few seconds after each change, and every minute while it is open. Everything goes (level, HP, ticks, effects, the fight, your edits); display settings, open tabs and the recent-changes list stay on each device. If two devices changed the same thing, the newer change wins and the other one is kept in Bring back.

      Bring back an earlier version

      Before changes from another device arrive, this iPhone keeps a copy of what it had (the last 10).

      Your GitHub key

      Sync needs your own key in every app, also to read: the sync repo is private. The key is saved only in this app on this iPhone, never in a file of the website.

      This key can read Skippy and Tom and change your website. Never share it and never paste it anywhere else.

      How to make or find the key
      1. Open github.com and sign in (a computer is easiest).
      2. Tap your picture (top right) › Settings › Developer settings (at the bottom of the left menu) › Personal access tokens › Fine-grained tokens. Open your key RPG Hub sync, or tap Generate new token for a new one.
      3. Repository access: Only select repositories › make sure rpghub-data is in the list.
      4. Permissions › Repository permissions › Contents › Read and write. (GitHub adds Metadata: read-only by itself.)
      5. A new key is shown only once: copy it (it starts with github_pat_). Write its end date down.
      6. Here, tap Paste key. Do the same once in every app on every device: Safari and the Home Screen app keep their own.

      Lost or leaked key: on the same GitHub page open the key and tap Delete, then make a new one.

      Combos

      If this happens, then do this. Twelve situations. Your numbers at level 5: HP 38 · AC 17 · DC 15 · attack +7 · slots 4 + 2.

      1 Start of a fight

      When: A fight is about to begin, and you have a turn or two to get ready.

      • Action Make your cannon. Hold woodcarver's tools. Pick flat ground within 5 ft. It has AC 18 and 25 HP. T p.17-18
      • Bonus action Activate it (you must be within 60 ft). Mourning Bell has no legs: it fires from your shoulder (one hand), or from where you set it down. Pick its type when you make it: Ballista, Flamethrower or Protector. T p.17-18
      • Reaction Keep it for Shield. AC 17 becomes 22. PHB p.275
      • Movement Step behind cover. PHB p.196
      free cannon (1st of the day)1 slot for a 2nd cannonmove 30 ft

      Example: Turn 1: you make Mourning Bell (action) and it fires at once (bonus action). You step behind a crate. Turn 2: Fire Bolt +7, 2d10 (+1d8 with the rod) (action). An enemy swings at you, so you cast Shield (reaction, 1 slot).

      2 Many enemies

      When: 3 or more enemies stand in a line or a clump, or crowd around you.

      • Action Once: make the cannon as a Flamethrower. T p.18
      • Bonus action Every turn: activate it. It sprays a 15-ft cone. Each enemy makes a DC 15 Dex save and takes 2d8 fire (half if it saves). Check that no friend stands in the cone. T p.18
      • Action If they crowd you: cast Thunderwave. 15-ft cube, DC 15 Con save, 2d8 thunder (+1d8 rod), failures pushed 10 ft. It also pushes friends, and it is loud. PHB p.282
      • Action Clumped further away: Shatter (level-2 slot). 10-ft sphere within 60 ft, DC 15 Con save, 3d8 thunder. PHB p.275
      • Movement Walk away. Pushed enemies spend movement to catch up.
      free cannon1 slot (Thunderwave or Shatter)bonus action each turn

      Example: Turn 1: the Flamethrower appears (action) and sprays (bonus action). Turn 2: Thunderwave (action, 1 slot) pushes the clump back. Mourning Bell sprays them again (bonus action). Turn 3: Fire Bolt +7 at the weakest enemy (action).

      3 One big enemy

      When: One strong enemy is alone and tough. It may pound your friends.

      • Action Once: make the cannon as a Force Ballista. T p.18
      • Bonus action Every turn: activate it. Spell attack +7, 2d8 force, push 5 ft. The target can be up to 120 ft from the cannon. T p.18
      • Action Every turn: Fire Bolt through the rod: +7, 2d10 + 1d8 fire. PHB p.242, T p.18
      • Action Instead, a slot: Faerie Fire so your whole team hits it with advantage (DC 15 Dex), or Scorching Ray (level-2 slot, 3 rays of 2d6), or Heat Metal if it wears metal. PHB p.239, p.273, p.250
      free cannonfree cantrip1 slot (Faerie Fire)concentration (Faerie Fire or Heat Metal)

      Example: Turn 1: the Ballista appears (action) and fires at once (bonus action). Turn 2: Fire Bolt (action) +7, 2d10 + 1d8. Mourning Bell fires (bonus action) for 2d8 and pushes it 5 ft. If both hit, that is about 24 damage in a round.

      4 Friend down (0 HP)

      When: A friend is at 0 HP, or several friends are hurt.

      • Movement Walk next to the friend, if needed.
      • Action Cast Cure Wounds by touch. It heals 1d8+4 and wakes them up. Too far? The homunculus can deliver it (its reaction, up to 120 ft from you). PHB p.230, T p.22 Out of slots? The healer's kit stabilizes at once (no HP back). PHB p.151
      • Bonus action If the cannon is a Protector, it gives 1d8+4 temp HP to friends within 10 ft. Temp HP do not wake a friend at 0 HP. T p.18
      • Reaction Keep it for Shield.
      1 slot (Cure Wounds)free cannonmove 30 ft

      Example: A friend drops to 0 HP. You walk to them (movement) and cast Cure Wounds (action, 1 slot). They get up. You have only one cannon at a time. To change its type, dismiss it (action), then make a new one (action, and 1 slot if it is your 2nd today). T p.17

      5 Enemy in my face

      When: An enemy stands next to you, or an attack roll would hit you.

      • Reaction Cast Shield when an attack would hit. +5 AC until your next turn, so AC 17 becomes 22. PHB p.275
      • Action Shocking Grasp: +7, 2d8 lightning. Advantage against a metal-armored target. The enemy cannot take reactions until its next turn. PHB p.275
      • Movement Walk away. If Shocking Grasp hit, the enemy has no reaction, so it gets no free hit as you leave. PHB p.195
      • Bonus action Activate the cannon (stay within 60 ft of it). Or Misty Step away (free once per long rest).
      1 slot (Shield)free cantripmove 30 ftcannon or Misty Step

      Example: A pirate swings at you. Shield (reaction, 1 slot) makes AC 22, and it misses. Your turn: Shocking Grasp (action) for 2d8. You walk back (movement). Mourning Bell fires (bonus action). Your dagger is weaker: +5, 1d4+2.

      6 Can't see or hit it

      When: The enemy is invisible, hiding, or hard to hit (high AC).

      • Action Cast Faerie Fire on the area. DC 15 Dex save. Outlined creatures glow, cannot hide, and attacks against them have advantage. PHB p.239
      • Bonus action The cannon attacks too, with advantage.
      • Action No slot: Shocking Grasp if the enemy wears metal. Or force a save with the Flamethrower (DC 15 Dex), Thunderwave or Shatter (DC 15 Con). No attack roll needed. T p.18, PHB p.282, p.275
      • Free Magical darkness or fog? Your darkvision may not help. Back into light and ask the DM what you can sense. PHB p.183
      1 slot (Faerie Fire)concentration, 1 minutefree cantrip

      Example: You hear a ghost-pirate you cannot see. Faerie Fire on its area (action, 1 slot, concentration). It glows. Your friends and Mourning Bell attack with advantage. If it hits you, roll Con +5 against DC 10, or half the damage if that is higher. PHB p.203

      7 Out of slots

      When: You have no spell slots left, or the cannon is gone.

      • Action Fire Bolt: +7, 2d10 (+1d8 with the rod). PHB p.242 Or Shocking Grasp if an enemy is close.
      • Bonus action Activate the cannon. This costs no slot if it is already made.
      • Action Other choices: Help (a friend gets advantage), Dodge, Disengage or Dash. PHB p.192
      • Movement Get behind cover. Cover gives +2 AC. PHB p.196
      • Free Shield is not possible now. Plan a long rest: short rests do not give slots back. PHB p.186
      free cantripfree cannonmove 30 ft

      Example: Your slots are gone. You step behind a barrel (movement), cast Fire Bolt (action), and Mourning Bell fires (bonus action). Next turn a friend flanks an enemy, so you use Help (action) to give them advantage.

      8 Exploring and talking

      When: No fight now. You search, read a map, sense magic, or talk.

      • Bonus action Send the homunculus ahead: it flies 30 ft, sees in the dark (60 ft), Perception +6, Stealth +5. Order it with your bonus action. T p.21-22
      • Free Ritual (10 extra minutes): cast Detect Magic with no slot. You sense magic within 30 ft while you concentrate. Then roll Arcana +7. PHB p.231, T p.12
      • Free Your skills: Investigation +7 to search, Intimidation +2 to scare. Cartographer's tools help with maps. PHB p.154
      • Free Missing a tool? The Right Tool for the Job makes one set of artisan's tools in 1 hour. It cannot make thieves' tools. The set vanishes when you use the feature again. T p.13
      no slotconcentration (Detect Magic)homunculustime: 10 min or 1 hour

      Example: A locked crypt door. You cast Detect Magic as a ritual (10 minutes, no slot) and sense a faint glow in the lock. Investigation +7 finds the trap. The homunculus flies down the corridor first and sees nobody waiting. The door opens. Do not start this just before a fight.

      9 Fire, cold or lightning hits me

      When: A breath, a spell or a trap is about to deal acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder damage to you.

      • Reaction Cast Absorb Elements (1 slot). You resist that damage type until the start of your next turn, so this hit is halved. It is from Xanathar's Guide, which is not in your books: ask your DM.
      • Free Not Shield: you have one reaction, and Shield does not help against a save-for-half breath. Shield is for attack rolls. Pick the right one.
      • Action Your next turn: the first melee hit you land deals +1d6 of the same damage type. Use Shocking Grasp (+7) or the Moon-touched dagger (+5, 1d4+2). Fire Bolt is not a melee attack, so it gets no bonus.
      • Bonus action The cannon fires as normal.
      1 slot (Absorb Elements)uses your reactionfree cantrip

      Example: A young dragon breathes fire on the party. You fail the save and would take 28. You cast Absorb Elements (reaction) and take only 14. On your turn you step next to it and Shocking Grasp it (action): the hit adds 1d6 fire. The cannon fires too (bonus action).

      10 Metal armor or a metal weapon

      When: An enemy wears metal armor or holds a metal weapon (a knight, a guard, a pirate with a cutlass), and its armor is too hard to hit.

      • Action Cast Heat Metal (level-2 slot, concentration). Pick a metal object you can see within 60 ft. It glows red-hot. Whoever holds or wears it takes 2d8 fire at once. There is no attack roll. PHB p.250
      • Free Their turn: if they hold it, they make a Con save (DC 15) or drop it. A creature that keeps it, or wears it, has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the start of your next turn.
      • Bonus action Next turns: burn them again for 2d8 fire, again with no roll. This is your bonus action, so the cannon does not fire that turn. Choose the better one: 2d8 sure fire damage, or the cannon's attack roll.
      • Action Shocking Grasp has advantage against metal armor: +7, 2d8 lightning. It also stops the enemy's reactions. PHB p.275
      1 level-2 slot (Heat Metal)concentration, 1 minutebonus action each later turn

      Example: A knight in plate (AC 18) shrugs off your friends' blows. Heat Metal (action) on his armor: 2d8 fire. He cannot take it off, so he has disadvantage on his attacks. Next turn, you burn him again (bonus action) and Shocking Grasp him with advantage (action). Do not cast Faerie Fire at the same time: you can keep only one concentration spell.

      11 Grabbed or boxed in

      When: Enemies hold you in a corner, a creature grapples you, or you must reach a ledge, a roof or the far side of a gap or locked door.

      • Bonus action Cast Misty Step. You vanish and appear up to 30 ft away, in a space you can see. You only need to speak: no hands. Fey Touched lets you cast it free once per long rest. After that it costs a level-2 slot. T p.79
      • Free Grappled? The jump takes you out of the grabber's reach, so the grapple ends. PHB p.290
      • Action You still have it. Fire Bolt a far target (120 ft), or Shocking Grasp from a better spot, or make the cannon again if it is gone.
      • Free Not the cannon: Misty Step is your bonus action, so the cannon does not fire this turn. Keep your reaction for Shield.
      free 1x per long restthen 1 level-2 slotbonus action30 ft jump

      Example: Two bandits corner you in an alley and one grabs your arm. You say the word: Misty Step (bonus action) puts you on a crate 30 ft away, free of the grab. Fire Bolt (action) hits the archer on the roof. Shield stays ready for your reaction.

      12 Dark place

      When: A cave, a ship's hold at night, or a crypt. Or you want to see (or hide) with care.

      • Free Darkvision 60 ft: you see gray shapes in the dark, but not colors. Friends without darkvision need light. PHB p.41
      • Free Draw the Moon-touched dagger. In darkness the drawn blade sheds moonlight: bright light 15 ft, dim light 15 ft more. Your friends can see by it. Sheathe it again to hide. It also shows where you are.
      • Free Small light: Magical Tinkering can make a coin glow, but only dim light 5 ft. T p.11
      • Action Something hides in the dark: Faerie Fire (DC 15 Dex, 1 slot, concentration) outlines creatures in the cube: they cannot hide, and attacks against them have advantage. PHB p.239
      • Bonus action Scout: the homunculus has darkvision 60 ft and Stealth +5. Order it with your bonus action. T p.21-22
      free: dagger, darkvision1 slot (Faerie Fire)concentration (Faerie Fire)homunculus

      Example: A cave with no torches. You draw the dagger (free): a pale glow, 15 ft bright, 15 ft dim. The homunculus flies ahead and sees a bat swarm. Then you sheathe the blade so you do not wake them. Later a shape moves in the dark: Faerie Fire outlines it for your friends. The Cloak of Billowing swishes for style only: use your bonus action for it only when the cannon is quiet.

      Slot budget

      You have 4 level-1 and 2 level-2 slots. Shield, Thunderwave, Cure Wounds, Faerie Fire, False Life and Absorb Elements cost a level-1 slot; Scorching Ray, Shatter and Heat Metal a level-2 slot. Misty Step and the Fey spell are free once each. A second cannon in one day costs a slot too. Plan them before the day starts. False Life (1d4+4 temp HP for 1 hour) is best just before a fight you can see coming. T p.17-18, PHB p.239

      Concentration

      Faerie Fire, Heat Metal and Detect Magic all use concentration. Casting a new one ends the old one. PHB p.203

      ActionBonus actionReactionMovementSlotConcentrationFree

      One bonus action, one reaction

      Your bonus action is for ONE of these each turn: fire the cannon, order the homunculus, Misty Step, burn Heat Metal again, or swish the Cloak of Billowing (style only, no rule effect). Your reaction is for ONE of these each round: Shield or Absorb Elements. The homunculus has its own reaction for Channel Magic. PHB p.189-190, T p.22

      Rules help

      The beginner basics, a glossary, the server's table rules and page numbers.

      Your turn, in one picture PHB p.189-190

      On your turn you get movement (30 ft), one action, maybe one bonus action, and you can talk a little. Once per round you also have one reaction, even on other people's turns.

      • Movement can be split: walk, act, walk again.
      • If you do not use the bonus action, nothing happens. For Skippy the bonus action is the cannon (or the homunculus, or Misty Step).
      • The reaction is for Shield.

      The d20 roll PHB p.7

      Almost everything is: roll a 20-sided die (d20), add a number, and compare with a target. Attack rolls beat the enemy's AC. Saves and checks beat a DC (difficulty number) the DM or the spell sets.

      Advantage and disadvantage PHB p.173

      Advantage: roll two d20 and keep the higher. Disadvantage: roll two and keep the lower. They cancel each other out. Faerie Fire gives your friends advantage. Shooting the crossbow next to an enemy gives you disadvantage.

      Check, save or attack? PHB p.174-179, p.194

      Ability check: you try something (search, climb, scare): d20 + skill. Saving throw: you resist something bad: d20 + save. Attack roll: d20 + attack bonus against AC. Your spells make enemies roll saves against your DC 15.

      Rests PHB p.186

      Short rest (1 hour): spend hit dice to heal (d8+2 each). Slots do NOT come back. Long rest (8 hours): full HP, all 6 slots, the free cannon, Misty Step and the Fey spell, Relentless Endurance, and half your hit dice come back.

      Dropping to 0 HP PHB p.197

      First, Relentless Endurance keeps you at 1 HP (once per long rest). After that you fall unconscious and roll death saves each turn: 10+ is a success, 3 successes = stable, 3 fails = dead. Any healing wakes you.

      Words A to C glossary

      AC (Armor Class): how hard you are to hit. Yours is 17.

      Action: the main thing you do on your turn.

      Attunement: a bond with a magic item. Max 3 items. Skippy needs none now.

      Bonus action: a small extra thing, only when a rule gives one. Yours: the cannon, the homunculus or Misty Step.

      Cantrip: a spell with no slot cost.

      Concentration: some spells last only while you focus. One at a time.

      Cover: half cover +2 AC, three-quarters +5.

      Words D to P glossary

      DC: difficulty number to reach on a roll. Your spells: 15.

      DM: Dungeon Master, the person who runs the game.

      Hit dice: dice you spend on a short rest to heal.

      Infusion: an artificer's magic put into a normal item.

      Initiative: roll at the start of a fight to set the turn order.

      Modifier: the small number from an ability score (Int 18 gives +4).

      Proficiency: being trained; add +3.

      Words R to Z glossary

      Reaction: one quick response per round, even on others' turns.

      Ritual: casting a spell 10 minutes slower, with no slot.

      Saving throw (save): a roll to resist something.

      Slot: fuel for a spell of level 1 or more. You have 4 level-1 and 2 level-2 per long rest.

      Temporary HP: extra HP that are lost first. They do not add up.

      Turn / round: a round is everyone's turn once, about 6 seconds.

      XP: experience points. Skippy has 6,900 (level 5).

      Proficiency bonus +3 PHB p.173

      Added to everything I am trained in: attacks, trained skills and saves, tools, spell DC.

      +3 at level 5.

      From Protector or False Life.

      The player's game server docs/TABLE-RULES.md

      • Unofficial Adventurers League. Rules are looser and may change.
      • D&D 5e 2014 rules. Start at level 3 (900 XP).
      • Anything official is allowed. No Unearthed Arcana.
      • Ability scores: standard array or rolled (reroll 1s). No point buy.
      • Do not build broken things: the DMs may veto for fun.
      • Faction Agent background: 3 renown and Rank 2 in a faction.
      • DMs may use soft homebrew rules and give homebrew items (approved by the DMs).

      Specifications docs/TABLE-RULES.md

      • Prerequisites: talk to a DM to fit them into the world.
      • You may reroll 1s on level-up hit points.
      • You may craft a unique background with a DM.
      • Setting-specific backgrounds are allowed; ask a DM if unsure.
      • Firearms exist but are uncommon, with their own proficiency (as in The Gunslinger).
      • Backup characters: one backup slot; see the server channel.

      What this means for Skippy docs/DECISIONS.md

      Level 5, 6,900 XP. Standard array. Tasha's custom origin (official, so allowed). Fey Touched feat at level 4: tell the DM. Crossbow and Fire Bolt, not a gun. Every choice has a DM answer card in Exceptions.

      If the DM asks

      Why do you have this? The DM's possible questions, one sentence to say, and where the rule is.

      Why is your Intelligence 17 on a half-orc?

      Say: I used Tasha's custom origin rule, so my half-orc gets +2 Intelligence and +1 Constitution instead of +2 Strength and +1 Constitution.

      If the DM says no: I use the book bonuses (Str +2, Con +1). Then my Int is 15 and my Str is 14. My spells get a little weaker.

      Tasha's p.7-8. The table allows anything official (table rule).

      Isn't a half-orc a strange pick for a smart class?

      Say: In the 2014 book a half-orc has no Intelligence penalty, and with Tasha's rule my bonus goes to Intelligence, so a half-orc inventor works fine.

      PHB p.40-41.

      Why are your scores 12, 14, 14, 17, 10 and 8?

      Say: I used the standard array (15, 14, 13, 12, 10, 8) and put 15 in Int, 14 in Dex, 13 in Con, 12 in Str, 10 in Wis and 8 in Cha, then added the origin bonuses.

      If the DM says no: I move the 12 to Wisdom or Charisma, because Strength is the score I need least.

      PHB p.13 for the array. The table allows the standard array or rolling, and no point buy (table rule).

      Why are you level 5 with 6,900 XP?

      Say: My server starts new characters at level 3 (900 XP), and my first adventure gave me 6,000 XP, so I have 6,900, which is level 5.

      Table rule. PHB p.15 (XP table).

      Why Fey Touched and not +2 Intelligence?

      Say: At level 4 I took the Fey Touched feat instead of the Ability Score Improvement: +1 Intelligence (17 to 18), Misty Step and one level-1 spell, each free once per long rest.

      If the DM says no: I take +2 Intelligence instead (19). The modifier stays +4, but I lose Misty Step and the extra spell.

      Tasha's p.79 (Fey Touched), p.13 (Ability Score Improvement). Feats need a talk with the DM (table rule).

      Why are you an Artillerist?

      Say: At level 3 an artificer picks a specialist, and I picked Artillerist because it gives me a cannon, 2 free spells and woodcarver's tools.

      Tasha's p.17-18.

      Why is your background Pirate if the book says Sailor?

      Say: Pirate is a variant of Sailor in the Player's Handbook, and I take Bad Reputation instead of Ship's Passage.

      If the DM says no: I use plain Sailor with Ship's Passage. Everything else stays the same.

      Good to know: Bad Reputation means people fear me, and in towns I can get away with small crimes. Please tell me how it works in your world.

      PHB p.139.

      Why is your alignment chaotic neutral?

      Say: Skippy is loyal to his crew and not to laws, so I chose chaotic neutral.

      Your own choice. The PHB has an alignment section (page not checked).

      Why does a half-orc know about dragons?

      Say: My captain, Edwine Blackscale, was a bronze dragonborn (battle soot darkened her scales, hence the name), and she raised me on her ship.

      Story only. No rule needed.

      Why do you speak Draconic and not Orc?

      Say: I swapped Orc for Draconic with Tasha's custom origin rule, because I grew up on a dragonborn captain's ship.

      If the DM says no: I keep Orc and drop Draconic. Then my languages are Common and Orc.

      Tasha's p.7. The DM may add or remove languages from the list.

      Why did you keep Intimidation?

      Say: It is the half-orc Menacing trait, and it fits a pirate with a bad reputation, so I did not swap it.

      PHB p.41. The optional swap is in Tasha's p.7-8, and I chose not to use it.

      Why cartographer's tools as your artisan's tools?

      Say: An artificer picks one set of artisan's tools, and I picked cartographer's tools because Skippy draws maps to find his captain.

      Good to know: I can also hold them to cast spells.

      Tasha's p.10.

      Why do you also know woodcarver's tools?

      Say: The Artillerist gives me woodcarver's tools for free, and I need them in my hand to make the cannon.

      Tasha's p.17.

      Why do you know navigator's tools and water vehicles?

      Say: They come with the Sailor background, and the Pirate variant keeps them.

      PHB p.139.

      Can you use guns? Why do you only have a crossbow?

      Say: Skippy uses a light crossbow, and I am not sure the artificer firearm line works at your table.

      If the DM says no: I stay with the crossbow and ask the DM what rules a pistol would use.

      DM approval needed. Tasha's p.10 has the firearm line. The table says firearms follow The Gunslinger subclass rules (table rule).

      Why 1,004 gold and two artisan's tools?

      Say: I bought woodcarver's tools for 1 gp before the game and made my cartographer's tools with The Right Tool for the Job (9 gp left), then my first adventure gave me 1,500 gp and I spent 505 gp on a breastplate, a 100 gp gem and a healer's kit.

      Good to know: I bought the woodcarver's tools off-scene while I made the character. The Right Tool for the Job takes 1 hour with thieves' or artisan's tools in hand. It makes one set of artisan's tools. The set is not magic, and it vanishes if I use the feature again.

      PHB p.154 (woodcarver's tools cost 1 gp), p.145 (breastplate 400 gp), p.151 (healer's kit 5 gp). Tasha's p.13 (The Right Tool for the Job), p.21 (the gem for the homunculus). PHB p.139 (sailor pouch, 10 gp).

      Where does the rest of your gear come from?

      Say: The Sailor background gives me a belaying pin, 50 ft of silk rope, a lucky charm (mine is a red coral horn) and common clothes, and the artificer gives me two simple weapons (spear and dagger), the crossbow and 20 bolts, studded leather, thieves' tools and a dungeoneer's pack. My first adventure added a Cloak of Billowing and a Moon-touched dagger, and I bought a breastplate.

      PHB p.139 (Sailor). Tasha's p.10 (artificer kit). PHB p.151 (packs). The two magic items are from Xanathar's Guide (the DM's reward).

      Why do you have Shield, Thunderwave, Scorching Ray and Shatter on top of your 6 spells?

      Say: They are Artillerist spells, so they are always prepared and do not count against my 6.

      Tasha's p.17.

      Why those 6 prepared spells?

      Say: Each day I prepare my Int modifier plus half my level, which is 4 + 2 = 6 spells, and I picked Cure Wounds, Faerie Fire, False Life, Detect Magic, Absorb Elements and Heat Metal.

      Tasha's p.11. Cure Wounds PHB p.230, Faerie Fire p.239, False Life p.239, Detect Magic p.231, Heat Metal p.250. Absorb Elements is in Xanathar's Guide (official, so allowed; ask the DM).

      Why Fire Bolt and not Guidance?

      Say: When an artificer gains a level, one cantrip can be swapped, so I swapped Guidance for Fire Bolt, which hits harder (2d10 at level 5, plus 1d8 through my rod).

      If the DM says no: I keep Guidance and use Shocking Grasp and the cannon for damage.

      Tasha's p.11 (cantrip swap), p.18 (Arcane Firearm). PHB p.242.

      Why do you cast spells while holding tools?

      Say: Artificers cast through tools, so I hold thieves' tools or an artisan's tool such as my cartographer's tools.

      Tasha's p.11 (Tools Required).

      Why can you cast Detect Magic with no spell slot?

      Say: Detect Magic is a ritual and I have it prepared, so I can cast it with 10 extra minutes and no slot.

      Tasha's p.12 (ritual casting). PHB p.231 (Detect Magic).

      Why did you drop Repeating Shot?

      Say: Each time I gain a level I may swap one infusion, so at levels 4 and 5 I swapped Repeating Shot and Enhanced Weapon for Homunculus Servant and Replicate Magic Item. My damage now comes from Fire Bolt and the cannon.

      If the DM says no: I keep Repeating Shot on the crossbow (+6, 1d8+3, no loading) and drop the homunculus.

      Tasha's p.12 (swap one infusion per level). Tasha's p.21-23 (the infusions).

      Why do you know 4 infusions but use only 2?

      Say: At level 5 I know 4 infusions and can keep 2 items infused, so I use Enhanced Defense on my breastplate and Homunculus Servant in a 100 gp gem, and I keep Mind Sharpener and Replicate Magic Item ready to swap in.

      Good to know: The homunculus acts right after my turn; it only Dodges unless I spend my bonus action to command it.

      Tasha's p.12 (Infuse Item). Tasha's p.21-23 (the infusions).

      Why does your cannon look like a small black iron ship's cannon?

      Say: When I make the cannon I choose its look, so mine looks like a tiny bell-shaped black iron ship's cannon with no legs, and I fire it from my shoulder like a rocket launcher. Black fits its name, Mourning Bell.

      If the DM says no: It looks like any other cannon. The numbers stay the same.

      Good to know: It is not a real ship's cannon. A real one is far too heavy to carry.

      Tasha's p.17-18. The look is flavor only. The rules allow any look.

      How do you make the cannon, and when?

      Say: I use an action with woodcarver's tools in my hand, and it appears in an empty spot within 5 ft, free once per long rest and then for a spell slot.

      Good to know: It lasts 1 hour, and I can have one cannon at a time.

      Tasha's p.17.

      Does the cannon act on its own?

      Say: No, I use a bonus action within 60 ft to make it act. Mine has no legs, so it never moves by itself.

      Tasha's p.17-18 (a cannon walks or climbs 15 ft only if it has legs).

      Why can you hold your cannon like a rocket launcher?

      Say: My cannon is Tiny, and a Tiny cannon can be held in one hand, so I carry it on my shoulder and it fires from there.

      If the DM says no: I put it on the ground next to me. The numbers stay the same.

      Good to know: While I hold it, one hand is busy: no crossbow (two hands). I set it down (free) and it keeps firing from there. On my shoulder the Flamethrower cone starts at me.

      Tasha's p.17 (Tiny cannon: held in one hand; you choose whether it has legs).

      Why is the cannon called Mourning Bell?

      Say: It is the last black iron gun of The Widow, and I named it Mourning Bell because it tolls for the lost crew.

      Story only. No rule needed.

      Why do you have 38 hit points?

      Say: I took the fixed average each level: 8 + 2 at level 1, then 5 + 2 at each of levels 2 to 5, which is 38 with Con +2.

      If the DM says no: I roll my hit dice and reroll any 1.

      Tasha's p.10. The table lets me reroll 1s if I roll (table rule).

      Why is your AC 17?

      Say: A breastplate gives 14, my Dex gives +2 (medium armor counts Dex up to +2), and the Enhanced Defense infusion gives +1.

      PHB p.145 (breastplate). Tasha's p.21 (Enhanced Defense).

      Why does AC 17 become 22 when you cast Shield?

      Say: Shield is a reaction that adds +5 AC until my next turn, so 17 becomes 22, and it uses a 1st-level slot.

      PHB p.275.

      Why a breastplate?

      Say: After my first adventure I bought a breastplate for 400 gp: medium armor with no disadvantage on Stealth, and with my Dex +2 it gives the full 14 + 2.

      PHB p.145 (armor table). Tasha's p.10 (artificers wear medium armor).

      Not checked: whether your DM allows Tasha's custom origin, and whether the artificer firearm line works at your table. Ask before the game.

      Roleplay

      How Skippy talks, acts and believes. A guideline, not a rulebook: take what is fun.

      Skippy in one look story

      A half-orc Artillerist artificer, level 5. A former powder monkey (the boy who runs gunpowder to the cannons) on the pirate ship The Widow. His captain, Edwine Blackscale (a bronze dragonborn), raised him. The ship sank. He is searching for her.

      His cannon, Mourning Bell, is a small bell-shaped black iron cannon. It has no legs and is Tiny. He fires it from his shoulder like a rocket launcher, or sets it down as a turret. It tolls for the lost crew. His lucky charm is a small red coral horn on a cord around his neck.

      His heart story

      Loyal (chaotic neutral). A crew is a family. He will break a law, but never a promise. He keeps his word like treasure. He hums the old songs of The Widow's crew. His flaw: he cannot stop looking at a blank map.

      The big idea: Skippy lost his ship, his captain and his crew. The old customs are how he holds on to them. His luck rituals are not silly to him. They are memory. Play them with a straight face and a small smile.

      His voice made up

      • Short and clear. A powder monkey learned to speak so people hear him over cannon noise.
      • Quick when he is excited, slow and quiet when he talks about the captain.
      • Clever, and he knows it. A small proud smile when he explains how something works. Then he looks at a map and forgets you.
      • Plain English and a few sea words. One sea word per scene is plenty. The luck is in what he does.

      How others see him made up

      The frightened: villagers step back, guards watch his hands. This is Bad Reputation at work.

      "I only bite on Tuesdays." (Then he checks it is not Tuesday.)

      The surprised: people expect a brute. He pulls out a chart and a spyglass.

      "Ah, you thought I'd smash it. I'm going to measure it."

      Pirate catchphrases made up

      • "Aye, skipper." (to anyone he trusts)
      • "Fair winds, shipmate."
      • "Belay that. I've got a better idea."
      • "I gave my word. That's the end of it."
      • "Powder, shot, match. In that order."

      Luck lines made up

      • "Touch iron." (before the cannon fires)
      • "Up anchor. The tide won't wait."
      • "Would you look at that."
      • "Whoever sets out, gets there." (before a risk)
      • "The sea gives and the sea takes." (after a loss)

      Sea words (a few are enough) real world

      aye = yes · avast = stop · belay that = forget that order · shipmate = crew friend · landlubber = someone who is not a sailor · fair winds = goodbye and good luck. A "yarr" now and then is fun. Not every sentence.

      The Widow's Articles made up

      Six short rules Skippy can quote. Real pirate crews swore to written "articles" (fair shares, no fighting aboard, a vote for big choices).

      • No one is left behind.
      • A promise given is a debt owed.
      • The powder is for the guns, not for fools.
      • The skipper's word is the tide.
      • The bell is rung for every one we lose.
      • A name is not sold.

      "Article two. I said I would carry it. So I carry it."

      Orc sayings he half-remembers made up

      • "A scar is a story you survived."
      • "Fire first, talk after. But never lie to a fire."
      • "The strong carry the loud, the loud carry the small."

      About his powder-burn scars: "Powder monkey. The cannon always bites back."

      Salt spilled at the tavern made up

      Set-up: a salt shaker tips over.

      "Left shoulder. Quick." (He throws a pinch.) "Now the devil's blind. Eat."

      A tiny scene, nobody waits for you.

      A black cat on the dock made up

      Set-up: a black cat crosses the party's path.

      "Wait. Let the cat go first. Cats know the way off a ship before we do."

      He makes the horns sign low, pointed at the ground. The DM may add a clue.

      Before firing Mourning Bell made up

      Set-up: any fight, when you activate the cannon.

      (swings Mourning Bell onto his shoulder, or sets it down like a turret; knocks twice on the black iron; one hand on the coral horn) "Touch iron. Sing, girl."

      Keep it under three seconds. After the first time, just knock.

      A stranger praises him made up

      Set-up: an NPC says "What a fine little cannon!"

      (grips the coral horn) "Don't. ... Say 'God bless it' and touch the iron. Compliments bring the eye."

      Leaving on a Tuesday made up

      Set-up: the party wants to leave at once, on the wrong day.

      "Not on Venus's day, not on Mars's day. Not to wed, not to go." (A pause.) "But the trail is warm. I'll go. I hold iron the whole road, and nobody whistles."

      He breaks his luck rule for the captain: his bond is stronger than his fear.

      A quiet moment made up

      When a friend or NPC dies, Skippy taps Mourning Bell once with his knuckle and says nothing. One tap per person lost. The best use of the cannon's name.

      No whistling on deck real world

      Sailors thought whistling could call up a wind, or a storm.

      Skippy hums but never whistles. "Stop. You'll wake the wind."

      Never rename a ship real world

      A named ship was thought to have its own spirit.

      "My name is the only thing the skipper gave me. I'll never change it. And you don't rename a boat."

      The ship's bell and the dead real world

      Bells marked time and were tied to death at sea.

      When someone falls, he taps Mourning Bell once. One tap per person lost.

      Coins for the drowned real world

      A coin under the mast for luck, a folk link to paying the ferryman of the dead.

      He presses an old coin from The Widow to the mast. "For the ones who didn't make it to shore."

      Davy Jones' locker real world

      A pirate name for the bottom of the sea.

      "She's in Davy's locker." Then: "No. She isn't. I'd feel it."

      Touch iron real world

      An old sailors' custom: touch iron, not wood, to push bad luck away. His best one, because Mourning Bell is black iron.

      Before he fires: "Touch iron," and two knocks on the barrel. It sounds like a tiny bell.

      Salt over the left shoulder real world

      Spilled salt: throw a pinch over the left shoulder, at the devil behind you.

      The horns sign and the red horn real world

      A hand sign (index and little finger up) and a small red horn charm against the evil eye. A charm should be a gift. Never point the horns sign at a person: he makes it toward the ground.

      "You don't buy your own. Somebody has to love you enough to give it."

      The evil eye real world

      The belief that an envious look, or a too-big compliment, brings harm. A folk test: drops of olive oil in a bowl of water. If the oil breaks up, the eye is there.

      An NPC praises the cannon: he touches iron and says "Bless it."

      Unlucky days, unlucky 17 real world

      No wedding and no voyage on Friday or Tuesday. In this custom 17 is the unlucky number, not 13.

      His Intelligence is 17: "Seventeen is unlucky. But it is my best number. Don't tell the sea." (The dice always stand.)

      Bread never upside down real world

      Bad luck to put a loaf crust-side down.

      He flips it quietly. "The sea knows."

      Saints and painted eyes real world

      He prays to Saint Rosalia for the sick and says Saint Francis of Paola's name when he crosses water. Painted eyes on a bow protect a boat.

      He chalks two small eyes on Mourning Bell. "So it sees where it's going."

      Bad Reputation at the table PHB p.139

      In towns, ordinary people are scared of him and let small crimes go. It is a story tool, not a dice roll.

      • Ask the DM: "Does anyone here know The Widow?"
      • Good side: a guard looks away, a shopkeeper stops haggling.
      • Bad side: a bounty hunter or an enemy captain may know the name too. That is a story gift.
      • Not for big theft, murder or arson.

      "I lean on the counter and say nothing. The Widow's name does the talking."

      Half-orc, raised by dragonborn PHB p.40-41

      People often fear half-orcs before they know them. Skippy never knew his parents. He grew up on a ship with dragonborn, speaks Draconic and has forgotten most of his Orc. He looks like an orc, talks like a dragonborn sailor, and belongs to The Widow.

      Orc gods (ask the DM) not your books

      Orcs honor Gruumsh, a one-eyed war god. Skippy does not have to follow him. Pick one: he never heard the orc gods (the sea was his church); he leans to Luthic (home, healing); or he fears the sea goddess.

      Safe in every world: "Skippy has heard of the orc war-god, and does not follow him."

      Edwine and clan honor PHB p.32-34

      Dragonborn are proud; clan and honor matter more than life. A bronze dragonborn breathes a line of lightning. "Blackscale" is a ship name, not her clan name: The Widow's crew became her clan, so she never left anyone behind.

      "The skipper said it in the old tongue. It means: the clan is the sea under your feet."

      Dragon gods (ask the DM) not your books

      Bahamut (justice) and Tiamat (greed). A pirate captain sits in between.

      "The skipper prayed to the silver one. I only prayed to her."

      Keep it fun made up

      Do: one custom per scene, ten seconds, invite friends in, let the dice stand, break a custom for the captain, tell the DM your plan.

      Do not: stop the fight for a ritual, refuse a group vote, mock a real faith, point the horns sign at people, keep an accent all evening.

      You do not need a voice. "Skippy knocks on the cannon and says 'touch iron'" is real roleplay.

      Labels: PHB / T = your books · not your books = lore from memory, ask the DM · real world = real folk custom (from the web, varies by family) · made up = an idea for Skippy you can change.

      Every time you level up

      • HP: roll 1d8 + CON, or take the average (5 + CON, which is 7 now). The table lets you reroll a 1. T p.10, PHB p.15
      • Swap one infusion for another one you could learn. Now known: Enhanced Defense, Mind Sharpener, Homunculus Servant, Replicate Magic Item. T p.12
      • Swap one cantrip for another artificer cantrip. T p.11
      • Prepared spells: you can change the list after a long rest. The count is INT mod + half your level, rounded down, at least 1. Always-prepared spells do not count. T p.11
      • Cannon: its HP is 5 × your level. Its damage goes up at level 9. T p.17-18
      • Hit dice: one more d8 each level, for short rests.

      Concentrating on Faerie Fire If I take damage: Con save +5, DC 10 or half the damage (the higher). Fail: it ends. A new concentration spell also ends it. PHB p.203
      Concentrating on Heat Metal If I take damage: Con save +5, DC 10 or half the damage (the higher). Fail: it ends. A new concentration spell also ends it. PHB p.203
      Concentrating on Detect Magic If I take damage: Con save +5, DC 10 or half the damage (the higher). Fail: it ends. A new concentration spell also ends it. PHB p.203
      Concentrating on Guidance If I take damage: Con save +5, DC 10 or half the damage (the higher). Fail: it ends. A new concentration spell also ends it. PHB p.203
      Concentrating on another spell If I take damage: Con save +5, DC 10 or half the damage (the higher). Fail: it ends. A new concentration spell also ends it. PHB p.203
      Blinded You cannot see. Checks that need sight fail. Attacks against you have advantage; your attacks have disadvantage. PHB p.290-292
      Charmed You cannot attack the one who charmed you or hit it with harmful magic. It has advantage on social checks with you. PHB p.290-292
      Deafened You cannot hear. Checks that need hearing fail. PHB p.290-292
      Frightened Disadvantage on ability checks and attacks while you can see the source of your fear. You cannot move closer to it on purpose. PHB p.290-292
      Grappled Your speed is 0. It ends if the grappler is incapacitated, or if something moves you out of its reach. PHB p.290-292
      Incapacitated You can take no actions and no reactions. PHB p.290-292
      Invisible No one can see you without magic or a special sense (noise and tracks still give you away). Attacks against you have disadvantage; your attacks have advantage. PHB p.290-292
      Paralyzed Incapacitated; you cannot move or speak. Strength and Dexterity saves fail. Attacks against you have advantage, and a hit from within 5 ft is a critical hit. PHB p.290-292
      Petrified Turned to stone with what you wear and carry. Incapacitated, cannot move or speak, unaware. Attacks against you have advantage; Strength and Dexterity saves fail. Resistance to all damage; poison and disease stop. PHB p.290-292
      Poisoned Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks. PHB p.290-292
      Prone You can only crawl, or stand up with half your movement. Your attacks have disadvantage. Attacks from within 5 ft have advantage; from farther away, disadvantage. PHB p.290-292
      Restrained Your speed is 0. Attacks against you have advantage; your attacks have disadvantage. Disadvantage on Dexterity saves. PHB p.290-292
      Stunned Incapacitated; you cannot move and can barely speak. Strength and Dexterity saves fail. Attacks against you have advantage. PHB p.290-292
      Unconscious Incapacitated, cannot move or speak, unaware. You drop what you hold and fall prone. Strength and Dexterity saves fail. Attacks against you have advantage, and a hit from within 5 ft is a critical hit. PHB p.290-292
      Exhaustion 1 Disadvantage on ability checks. PHB p.291
      Exhaustion 2 Disadvantage on ability checks; Speed halved. PHB p.291
      Exhaustion 3 Disadvantage on ability checks; Speed halved; Disadvantage on attacks and saves. PHB p.291
      Exhaustion 4 Disadvantage on ability checks; Speed halved; Disadvantage on attacks and saves; Hit point maximum halved. PHB p.291
      Exhaustion 5 Disadvantage on ability checks; Speed halved; Disadvantage on attacks and saves; Hit point maximum halved; Speed 0. PHB p.291
      Exhaustion 6 Disadvantage on ability checks; Speed halved; Disadvantage on attacks and saves; Hit point maximum halved; Speed 0; Death. PHB p.291
      Bane Subtract 1d4 from my attack rolls and saving throws. Lasts while the caster concentrates, up to 1 minute. PHB p.216
      Faerie Fire on me I glow. Attacks against me have advantage, and I cannot be invisible. Up to 1 minute. PHB p.239
      Shield (my spell) +5 AC until the start of my next turn, also against the attack that hit me. Magic Missile does nothing to me. PHB p.275
      Bless Add 1d4 to my attack rolls and saving throws. Lasts while the caster concentrates, up to 1 minute. PHB p.219
      Shield of Faith +2 AC. Lasts while the caster concentrates, up to 10 minutes. PHB p.275

      Rest and hit dice

      Short rest (1 hour)

      Hit dice used d8+2 each
      Relentless Endurance used once per long rest

      Slots, free cannon and Relentless on Play: filled = ready, hollow = used. Short rest: roll one hit die (d8+2), type the total, tap the button. Repeat for more dice. Slots do not come back.

      Long rest (8 hours)

      A ticked box is used until the rest. Long rest: everything comes back, plus half your hit dice (at least 1). PHB p.186

      A long rest brings back: full HP, all spell slots, the free cannon, Relentless Endurance, 1 hit die, exhaustion −1. Temp HP, concentration, spell effects, the cannon and the fight end. Conditions stay.
